text:
marta (PM): Quick sync — Sales flagged 3 enterprise prospects asking for multi-region failover + per-tenant isolation guarantees before signing. Need a concise launch gating checklist we can send them.

alex (eng-arch): +1. What's the acceptable SLA band they're asking for?

liz (sales-eng): They want 99.95% availability across two regions, data residency in EU for one customer, and a fallback policy that keeps latency under 200ms for 95p of requests.

ben (product): That's tight but doable if we scope the pilot: 1) partner customers only, 2) canary rollout, 3) documented fallback rules.

sam (sre): Operationally we need clear runbook items: automated failover test, capacity reservation per-tenant, and telemetry to detect cross-region traffic surges.

marta (PM): Proposal for launch gating checklist draft: 1) SLA target + verified test plan, 2) Pilot cohort (n=2 customers), 3) Isolation config (network + KV cache), 4) Routing policy spec + deterministic fallback, 5) Pricing/commitment for reserved capacity. Thoughts?

alex (eng-arch): Suggest adding a model-variant fallback mapping in the routing policy — e.g., when primary region overloaded use a quantized, lower-cost model in secondary region. Include compatibility matrix.

liz (sales-eng): Sales will accept a staged commitment if we provide a playbook and an escalation path. They asked for a sample contract clause for capacity outages.

ben (product): I'll draft a short clause. We should also call out expected per-token cost delta when using fallback model. Customers want transparency.

sam (sre): For the runbook we need automated chaos tests: simulate region loss, validate KV cache warm-up time, measure p95 latency to secondary. Can we define the test harness now?

alex (eng-arch): Sketch of routing policy snippet (for the doc):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  primary_region: eu-west-1
  fallback_sequence:
    - region: eu-west-1
      model_variant: redwood-v2-opt
    - region: us-west-2
      model_variant: redwood-v2-quantized
  criteria:
    - metric: request_latency_p95
      threshold_ms: 200
    - metric: region_capacity_pct
      threshold: 85
```

marta (PM): Nice. Add a line about data residency: requests with residency=EU must not cross into non-EU regions except in documented disaster mode and with explicit customer consent.

liz (sales-eng): Also add an onboarding checklist for customer engineers: provide sample traffic profile, pin model versions, and acceptance test suite run results.

ben (product): Prioritization question for the roadmap: do we treat this as Q2 pilot (high touch) or Q3 GA (self-serve)? My vote: Q2 pilot, ramp Q3 if metrics look good.

alex (eng-arch): Agree. We need engineering spikes: routing policy DSL, KV cache eviction semantics across regions, and an autoscaling floor for dedicated pools. Rough estimate: 6 engineer-weeks across infra + runtime.

sam (sre): Add monitoring alerts: cross-region latency spike, cache-thrashing rate, and fallback usage counter. Tie to on-call runbooks.

marta (PM): Action items: @alex build draft routing DSL + compatibility matrix (due in 5 days); @ben draft contract clause and cost delta note (3 days); @sam prototype chaos runbook (7 days); @liz gather two pilot customers and traffic profiles (ASAP). I'll collate into a one-pager.

oncall-bot: Deployed canary pipeline #347 to staging — build d4b2a1.

liz (sales-eng): Thanks — will push customers to commit to pilot by EOW.

ben (product): One-pager outline: Context, Launch gates, Operational responsibilities, Customer onramp checklist, Pricing/commitment. I'll share first draft tomorrow.

alex (eng-arch): Quick question — is cross-region KV cache warming acceptable as part of the canary, or do we require cold-start validation too?

sam (sre): Both. Cold-start tests for worst-case, warm-path for common-case. We'll include measurements in the acceptance criteria.

marta (PM): Perfect. If no blockers, I'll turn this into a product ticket and tag docs + legal for the contract language.

liz (sales-eng): :thumbsup:

ben (product): +1.

alex (eng-arch): +1.

sam (sre): +1.
